Inglewood, California
  January 30, 2024

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  January 30, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
  of 2:01 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Gray, Morales,
  Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member Padilla.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
  on the Agendas.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated January
  26, 2024, in the amount of $7,382,904.64, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor
  Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Gray, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla.

142  RESOLUTION NO. 24-30 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024
  OPERATING BUDGET. Staff report dated January 30, 2024, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution amending the Fiscal
  Year 2023-2024 Operating Budget to carry over prior year encumbrances into the current
  fiscal year.
 January 30, 2024

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 24-30 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2023-2024 ANNUAL BUDGET TO ROLL
  PRIOR YEAR ENCUMBRANCES INTO THE CURRENT FISCAL YEAR

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

160  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – IT’S YOUR PARTY FLORAL & EVENT DESIGN.
  Staff report dated January 30, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and
  Council Members authorize payment of an invoice submitted by It’s Your Party Floral &
  Event Design for providing set-up, signage, and décor for the City’s Annual Turkey
  Giveaway on November 21, 2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $2,622.40. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

183  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – MEHTA MECHANICAL COMPANY, INC DBA
  MMC, INC. Staff report dated January 30, 2024, was presented recommending that the
  Mayor and Council Members authorize payment of the final invoice submitted by Mehta
  Mechanical Company, Inc. dba MMC, Inc. (Contractor), to close out the North Inglewood
  Booster Pump No. 3 Replacement Project, per Bid No. CB-23-05.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $4,895.78. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

131.8  AGREEMENT NO. 24-111 APPROVED – SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA HOUSING
  RIGHTS CENTER, INC. (HRC). Staff report dated January 30, 2024, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve an agreement with the
  Southern California Housing Rights Center, Inc. (HRC), to provide fair housing counseling
  and housing discrimination services for Fiscal Year 2023-2024.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 24-111 in an amount not to exceed
  $64,500. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

183&205  ORDINANCE NO. 24-04 ADOPTED - AMENDING CHAPTER 3 OF THE
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO DESIGNATE CITY-OWNED PARKING
  FACILITIES AS PARKING METER ZONES, AND ESTABLISHING SPECIAL
  EVENT PARKING RATES AND FINES FOR ON-STREET AND OFF-STREET
  PARKING METER ZONES. Staff report dated January 30, 2024, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members adopt Ordinance No. 24-04,
  designating City-owned Parking Facilities as Parking Meter Zones and establishing Special
  Event Parking Rates and fines for On-street and Off-street Parking Meter Zones.

  2
 January 30, 2024

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Faulk that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  Ordinance No. 24-04 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  AMENDING CHAPTER 3 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  DESIGNATE CITY-OWNED PARKING FACILITIES AS PARKING METER
  ZONES, ESTABLISH VARIABLE SPECIAL EVENT PARKING METER
  RATES, AND ESTABLISH PARKING FINES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF

  which was introduced at the meeting held on January 9, 2024, be adopted. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

101  REPORTS – CITY MANAGER. City Manager Mark F. Weinberg reported the
  unanimous concurrence of the Mayor and City Council for the appointment of Sylvia
  Fernandez as the City’s Human Resources Director. He provided some background
  history and mentioned their attendance at Bell Gardens High School. Finally, he
  addressed her education and his pleasure in discussing how to move the department
  forward.

126  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson congratulated Sylvia
  Fernandez on her appointment as the City’s new Human Resources Director. She mentioned
  that Sylvia was very instrumental in walking her through the process to ensure everything
  was taken care of when her parents had passed.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning his 53-foot-wide trailer parked on Beach
  Street, which was recently towed for being there for 72 hours. He stated that his trailer
  was also recently towed in Los Angeles and was held for three weeks, which cost him
  $1,400 to get it back. He also stated that he was not a truck driver but was building a
  business inside the trailer. The speaker discussed that after retrieving the trailer from
  being towed in Los Angeles, he moved it closer to his house on Beach Street, about half a
  mile from Bryant's Tow. He also discussed not paying attention to the markings on the tires
  and watching Bryant's Tow take his trailer. The speaker noted that he had gone to get  his
  trailer the next day, and a receipt was made out for $1,300 to get it out, not even 24  hours
  later. Also, he addressed that Bryant's Tow wasn't equipped to lift the trailer, so they
  subcontracted a Los Angeles towing company to do the work. According to his
  paperwork, he mentioned that the towing company in Los Angeles took three and a half
  hours to pick up the trailer, which was eight miles away. He also noted that he had been
  trying to fight this by himself, but there was no one to govern Bryant's Tow, which the
  City represents. The speaker expressed his feelings of being hurt because when he looks
  at the towing company, he looks at the City that represents this company. Furthermore, he
  added that the towing company was skyrocketing prices and taking advantage of people.
  The speaker also added that so many things were happening and that it was a reflection of
  the city. Finally, he reiterated that he didn't know how to fight his complaint
  correctly and wanted someone with compassion to understand and help him.

  3
 January 30, 2024

  Speaker (Name Unknown) acknowledged the great City of Inglewood. He stated that he
  knew that sometimes he gets on the Mayor’s nerves when talking about the City of Los
  Angeles, and he gave his reasoning for doing so. He mentioned that it was because Los
  Angeles surrounds Inglewood, and their policies affect Inglewood. Finally, he requested
  that the Mayor to collaborate with the Mayor of Los Angeles regarding her policy.

  After Council Comments, Mayor Butts reopened the Public Comment portion at the
  hour of 2:21 p.m.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke about her life being a nightmare since purchasing her
  home in Inglewood. She stated that Code Enforcement violated her privacy because they
  showed up at her house because of illegal construction. Additionally, she stated she was
  painting and cleaning and was not violating her permit. She discussed how Code
  Enforcement Officers took pictures, issued her a citation, and made an appointment
  to apply for the necessary permit. She also discussed her life's difficulty because of the
  violation and the rules being changed. She also mentioned applying for a permit for her
  kitchen cabinets and contacting multiple contractors to request quotes. She addressed
  receiving another visit from Code Enforcement while the contractors were there and
  reported feeling harassed. Finally, she also addressed submitting her applications, which
  weren’t accepted, making her life miserable.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in memory of Margaret Bowers, a former President of the School Board, at the
  hour of 2:24 p.m.

  Approved this 9th day of April, 2024.
  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
